absent: PMU operations for read, enable, disable and scheduling beyond gating conditions.
Full layouts of event, context, processor context and grouping structures beyond referenced fields.
Scheduler, interrupt and timer subsystem behavior behind forwarding, arming and remote invocation.
Reference counting, RCU, spinlock, mutex and memory ordering primitives.
Cgroup identity, lookup and time accounting details.
Sample data layout and user ABI numeric values for formats and sample flags.

findings.text: Without optional grouping support, association always succeeds, time contributions are absent, establishment is rejected as invalid, and enablement, switching and time propagation have no observable effect.

With grouping support, activation applies only to member events, maintains per unit and per context membership tallies, and the first activation within a context associates processor scope with the grouping derived from the current execution entity.

Multiplex advancement remains quiescent unless a need marker is set for processor or task scope; when needed it proceeds under combined context protection with measurement quiesced, refreshes flexible scheduling and advances order while leaving pinned membership undisturbed, and reports whether advancement occurred. Timer handling re-arms on advancement and otherwise marks the timer idle under dedicated protection with interrupts excluded.

Advancement candidacy prefers active flexible membership and otherwise selects the earliest ordered grouping entry, handling processor bound and task bound contexts separately with fallback between unbound and processor specific lookup, and always clears the need marker with later admission free to set it again.

Grouping entries live in an ordered tree keyed by processor identity, performance unit identity, grouping identity and insertion sequence, with absent groupings ordered before present ones and present ones ordered by numeric identity; lookup supports full ordering and subtree probes that disregard trailing key components.

Collection insertion assigns a fresh increasing sequence value, while removal checks membership and resets the detached entry to an unlinked condition with cleared sequence; empty collections start with a vacant tree and zero sequence.

Multiplex timing relies on dedicated spin protection for activity state and interval. Initialization establishes a sane default interval and a pinned monotonic handler, while restart only arms an idle timer by advancing expiration one interval, including a remote invocation wrapper with identical effect.

Context lifetime uses reference counting with deferred reclamation. Final release cascades to ancestor contexts and associated execution entities except for tombstone markers, while non-final release orders against waiters and wakes tombstone waiters.

Stable mutex acquisition tolerates concurrent context reassignment by holding a reference obtained under read side protection, revalidating identity after locking and retrying on mismatch; release pairs unlocking with reference drop and a non-nested convenience cover exists.

Task context capture disables interrupts across read side lookup to respect nesting beneath scheduler protection, confirms the installed context is unchanged after acquiring spin protection, rejects tombstone or dying instances, and pinning adjusts a usage tally under interrupt safe spin protection.

Time evaluation yields nothing without a context, delegates for grouping members, and otherwise selects between a stable snapshot and a live computation according to activity state. Type classification derives pinned versus flexible nature from the group leader and adds a processor scope marker for contexts without a task, requiring spin protection.

Attachment records context membership and arrival time, enrolls only leaders in pinned or flexible collections according to attributes, and maintains totals for membership, user readable counters, statistics inheritance, inheritance read interaction, per unit membership and generation, activating grouping for enabled events. Detachment reverses all tallies and tolerates repeated removal.

Read and sample footprints derive from format and sample selections plus sibling counts, with grouped reads including a count word and identifier options enlarging per entry size. Validation rejects prospective growth beyond sixteen kilobytes across the newcomer, leader and siblings, while fresh leaders skip sibling review. Initial state is off when disabled and otherwise inactive.
Sibling enrollment is idempotent, folds capabilities into the leader, appends at the tail with updated sibling and generation tallies, and refreshes computed footprints for leader and every sibling.
The default multiplex interval equals one thousand divided by the system tick rate.
Rotation assumes membership totals are stable because it runs where new installation is impossible.
Auxiliary routing reports absence unless the sink offers auxiliary capability and the source unit supplies a matching predicate, in which case the predicate outcome governs.
Context locking, task pinning, grouping manipulation and attach management are available as shared services across compilation scope with defined locking and lifetime expectations.
Traversal support includes filtered iteration for a given processor and performance unit plus exhaustive ordered walks over every node in a collection.
Hardware read delegation occurs only while the event resides in active state; otherwise observation is a no-op.

Separation from ancestry clears the parent link under spin protection, advances generation and returns the prior parent. Process and thread identity resolve through the topmost ancestor inside the creation namespace with a sentinel for absent identities of non-live entities, and primary identity prefers ancestor identity when present.
